# Purpose

The script `retail_analysis.R` examines synthetic retail transactions and summarizes revenue by product category.

## Inputs

| Field | Meaning | Imported type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Transaction_ID | Transaction identifier | Character |
| Sales_Date | Transaction date | Character |
| Category | Product category | Character |
| Quantity | Units sold | Integer |
| Unit_Price | Unit price | Integer |

## Dependencies

The analysis uses base R. Rendering this document requires R Markdown and Pandoc.

## Workflow

### Import and inspection

The CSV is imported into `sales`. The student inspected its structure and checked missing values and duplicate rows in the Console.

```{r inspection, eval=FALSE}
head(sales)
str(sales)
colSums(is.na(sales))
sum(duplicated(sales))
```

### Revenue and summary

The following lines reproduce the code visible in the student's executed script. Revenue is quantity multiplied by unit price; `sum` totals revenue and `aggregate` groups it by category.

```{r summary, eval=FALSE}
sales$Revenue <- sales$Quantity * sales$Unit_Price
total_revenue <- sum(sales$Revenue)
print(total_revenue)
category_revenue <- aggregate(Revenue ~ Category, data = sales, FUN = sum)
print(category_revenue)
```

### Visualization

The bar chart displays category revenue with descriptive axis labels.

```{r chart, eval=FALSE}
barplot(category_revenue$Revenue,
        names.arg = category_revenue$Category,
        main = "Revenue by Product Category",
        xlab = "Product Category",
        ylab = "Revenue ($)",
        col = "steelblue")
```

## Outputs

| Category | Revenue ($) |
| --- | ---: |
| Clothing | 390 |
| Electronics | 820 |
| Groceries | 220 |
| Home | 405 |
| **Overall** | **1,835** |
